title: Privileged Action Audit Record Format and Taxonomy for RBAC v2
creator: Kemi Adeyemi
description:
Problem: RBAC v2 introduces richer intent and policy primitives (roles, grants, scoped delegations). Current audit logs are inconsistent across admin UIs, SAML actions, and programmatic changes. We need a single, searchable, retention-friendly record format and taxonomy that captures both human and system-initiated privileged actions, encodes object-level diffs, and preserves SSO/SAML provenance for forensic and compliance use cases.

Goals: Provide a concrete event envelope and field set that: (1) unambiguously records actor identity and assertion provenance (SAML/OIDC/SCIM/Service-Account), (2) captures target objects and before/after diffs in a compact, query-friendly way, (3) supports sampling and redaction policies, (4) enables backward-compatible migration from v1 audit streams, and (5) enables efficient storage + retrieval for RBAC-focused queries (who changed role X, when was permission Y granted, link to session/trace).

Proposed event envelope (high-level): Single-line JSON envelope persisted to audit store with the following top-level fields. Note: field names chosen for clarity and stable indexing; values left as primitive or stringified structures to avoid deep nested schema in the store.

- event_id: stable UUID v4 for traceability and idempotency.
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601 timestamp when action was applied.
- event_type: taxonomy keyword (see taxonomy section) e.g., role_grant.create, role_grant.revoke, policy.update, delegation.create, sso.link, service_account.rotate.
- actor_type: human | service | system | external_idp
- actor_id: canonical internal identifier (user:12345, svc:env-prod-12)
- actor_identity_source: assertion source string (saml:acme-enterprise, oidc:google, scim:okta, internal)
- actor_session: session id or trace id (if available) to correlate with request logs
- target_type: principal | role | policy | resource | delegation | key
- target_id: canonical id for the object acted on (role:billing-admin)
- change_kind: create | update | delete | action | link | unlink
- delta_encoding: compact-diff-v1 | snapshot (indicates how change_payload should be interpreted)
- change_payload: stringified compact diff or snapshot (see delta section)
- justification: free-form text (user-supplied reason or automated reason)
- risk_level: low | medium | high | unknown (optional operator-assigned)
- correlated_events: comma-separated event_ids for multi-step flows (optional)
- retention_class: default | pii_sensitive | regulatory_7y (controls downstream retention)
- system_tags: comma-separated internal flags (eg: migrated_from_v1, replayed)
- raw_assertion: optional base64(saml_assertion) when legal/retention allows (usually redacted)
taxonomy: We propose a hierarchical taxonomy to drive event_type and enable rollups in dashboards and queries. Top-level categories: admin_change, identity_link, auth_flow, policy_engine, key_mgmt, system_maintenance. Examples: admin_change.role_grant.create, admin_change.role_grant.revoke, admin_change.policy.update, identity_link.sso.provision, identity_link.sso.deprovision, auth_flow.session.login, policy_engine.evaluation.override, key_mgmt.rotate, system_maintenance.schema_migration. Each type must map to a suggested retention class and a set of required fields (actor_identity_source required for identity_link.*, change_payload required for admin_change.*).
delta_format_and_guidance:
Two supported encodings: compact-diff-v1 and snapshot. Compact-diff-v1 uses a small change-frame with explicit ops: add/replace/remove on normalized fields (eg: permissions:[+read], grants:[+role:role-xyz], metadata.name:replace). The diff is represented as a semicolon-delimited list of ops to keep payloads small and make token-level indexing possible. Snapshot is a full stringified representation of the object after change, used when diffs are hard to compute or for initial seeds. Guidance: Use compact-diff for role/policy edits; use snapshot for delegation or resource creation. Diffs should include attribute paths, old_value (stringified) when allowed, and new_value. When old_value contains PII or secrets, set retention_class to pii_sensitive and redact old_value or omit it.
Examples: compact-diff-v1 payload examples: "permissions:[+read,-write];grants:[+role:billing-admin];metadata.display_name:replace='Billing Admin'".
For large array diffs prefer ops grouped by field to avoid O(n) diffs for stable order lists.
ssO_and_saml_provenance: SSO/SAML considerations: Always record actor_identity_source and link actor_id to canonical user if available. If SAML assertion is present, record assertion_id, idp_entity, and assertion_signature_digest (sha256) when retention rules prohibit storing the full assertion. Where customers request forensic exports, raw_assertion may be included under restricted retention. Map SAML NameID and persistent attributes to actor_id mapping table at ingestion time; ingestion should also persist idp-attribute-hints as searchable tags for downstream lookup. For SCIM-provisioned changes include scim_job_id and external_provisioner in system_tags.
redaction_and_sampling_policy: Redaction rules: default redact sensitive attributes in old_value (passwords, secret_keys, credential_material, full_saml_assertion) and replace with <REDACTED:reason>. Sampling: low-sensitivity events (auth_flow.session.login success) may be sampled 1:100 during low-load windows; high-risk admin_change.* events must never be sampled. Use retention_class to drive automatic downstream scrubbing and archival regimes. Audit ingestion must validate retention_class and reject events lacking required retention annotations for regulated targets.
backwards_compat_and_migration: Migration strategy from v1: run parallel ingestion for 90 days. Provide translation layer that maps old event_type values to new taxonomy and populates actor_identity_source where possible. Mark migrated events with system_tags:migrated_from_v1 and preserve original_event_id in correlated_events. Provide a backfill job to compute compact-diff-v1 for older role edits where possible, otherwise store snapshot with migration_reason tag.
storage_and_query_considerations:
Storage model: append-only ledger (immutable files) with secondary index tables for event_type, actor_id, target_id, timestamp range. Keep change_payload as a compressed blob but also emit tokenized searchable terms for role names, permission names, and idp hints as top-level indexable fields. For analytic workloads, provide daily denormalized materialized views for RBAC audits (eg: role_grants_by_user).
Query patterns prioritized: find all role grants for user X, show timeline of policy changes to Y, list SAML link events for idp Z. Make sure retention_class filters are enforced at query time to prevent accidental export of PII.
open_questions_and_decisions:
- Should we extend event_type to allow vendor-specific suffixes (eg: key_mgmt.rotate.aws_kms)? Proposal: allow vendor suffix but require canonical mapping in docs.
- How do we represent batch operations (eg: reconcile roles for 10k users)? Proposal: emit one event per logical change and a parent batch event that lists child event_ids to simplify query and limits event size.
- How to enforce signing/envelope integrity? Proposal: store event_id with HMAC signature at write time and surface signature in correlated storage for tamper-detection.
- Rollout plan: phased ingestion with feature flag to enable compact-diff detection in runtime for role edits.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ingestion accepts the new envelope with either delta_encoding values and indexes event_type, actor_id, target_id and timestamp.
2) Kibana/Console can render a timeline for admin_change.* events showing compact diffs as human-readable ops.
3) Migration job can translate v1 events and mark migrated events with system_tags.
4) Redaction pipeline enforces retention_class and strips/obfuscates disallowed fields.
5) SSO/SAML provenance fields are populated for actions originating from IdP flows.
6) Performance: ingestion latency for audit events remains <250ms P50 and <1s P95 under steady load.
